description: An index-free getelementptr returns its pointer operand unchanged, preserving the original pointer value and type.
Return the base pointer when pointer result type is unchanged and every GEP index is zero (the all-zero GEP no-op).
extra: vector result type must equal the pointer type; prevents erasing a vector splat

description: A GEP with a poison base pointer or any poison index yields poison of the computed GEP result type.
If the base pointer is undef, produce undef of the computed GEP result type.
For a non-scalable, sized source element type with exactly one GEP index, return the pointer when the type's allocation size is zero and the pointer result type is unchanged.

Fold gep(base, sub(ptrtoint(P), ptrtoint(base))) to P when the source element allocation size is 1, index scalar width is at least address width, P has the GEP result type, and P/base have the same underlying object.

Fold gep(base, ashr(sub(ptrtoint(P), ptrtoint(base)), C)) to P when allocation size equals 2^C, index width covers address width, P's type equals the GEP result type, and P/base have the same underlying object.
extra: shift amount must select exact allocation-size power of two

description: Fold gep(base, sdiv(sub(ptrtoint(P), ptrtoint(base)), allocation_size)) to P when there is one index, the element is sized and non-scalable, index width covers address width, P has the result type, and P/base have the same underlying object.

For a non-scalable GEP whose final indexed type has allocation size 1, whose preceding indices are zero, and whose last index width equals the pointer index width, fold gep(gep(V,C), sub(0, ptrtoint(strippedBase))) to inttoptr(accumulatedBaseOffset); require nonzero accumulated offset.
extra: strip and accumulate inbounds constant offsets
pointer provenance caveat: avoid inttoptr zero

description: Under the same unit-sized final type, zero preceding indices, and matching index width conditions, fold gep(gep(V,C), xor(ptrtoint(strippedBase), -1)) to inttoptr(accumulatedBaseOffset - 1); require accumulated offset not equal to one.
extra: strip and accumulate inbounds constant offsets
pointer provenance caveat: avoid inttoptr zero

description: When base pointer and all indices are constants, build a constant GEP and use ConstantFoldGetElementPtr if ConstantExpr construction fails.
When base pointer and all indices are constants and ConstantExpr construction succeeds, fold the resulting constant expression with ConstantFoldConstant.
For constant aggregate and constant inserted value, constant-fold insertvalue at the specified index path.
insertvalue(Agg, poison, indices) returns Agg; if inserted value is undef, also return Agg only when Agg is guaranteed non-poison.
Cancel insertvalue(Agg, extractvalue(Y, indices), indices) to Y when aggregate operand types and index paths match and Agg is poison, or Agg is undef while Y is guaranteed non-poison.
extra: matching aggregate type and full index path

description: Cancel insertvalue(Agg, extractvalue(Agg, indices), indices) to Agg when aggregate operand type and index paths match and both use the identical SSA aggregate.
extra: matching aggregate type and index path

description: For constant vector, value, and lane index, fold insertelement as a constant expression.
For a fixed-length vector, a constant lane index greater than or equal to its element count makes insertelement poison.
An undef insertelement lane index may choose an out-of-range index, so the result is poison.
insertelement(Vec, poison, Idx) returns Vec; undef inserted value also returns Vec only if Vec is guaranteed non-poison.
If the constant input vector is a splat of the constant inserted value, inserting that same value at any lane returns the original vector.
Cancel insertelement(Vec, extractelement(Vec, Idx), Idx) to Vec when both vector and index operands are the same SSA values.
For a constant aggregate, constant-fold extractvalue at the specified index path.
For extractvalue of a chain of insertvalue operations, return the inserted value when the extract path exactly matches the inserted path; stop if a common prefix is a proper prefix of either path.
For extractvalue(umul_with_overflow(X,1), 0), return X; requires a single aggregate index selecting result element zero and either multiplication operand to be one.

For extractvalue(umul_with_overflow(X,1), 1), return false of the comparison result type; requires a single aggregate index selecting overflow result element one and either multiplication operand to be one.
For constant vector and constant lane index, fold extractelement as a constant expression.
If the vector operand is undef and the index is constant, return undef of the vector element type.
An undef extractelement index may select an out-of-range lane, so the result is poison of the vector element type.
For a fixed-length vector, a constant index out of bounds makes extractelement poison.
For an in-bounds constant lane index, if the input vector is a splat, return its splat element.
For a constant lane index, return the scalar previously inserted at that lane when recursive vector inspection finds it.
Cancel extractelement(insertelement(Vec, Elt, Idx), Idx) to Elt when the index is not a constant and the exact same SSA index operand is used.
For a nonconstant index, if the input vector is a splat, return its splat element.
If all non-self PHI inputs are undef, poison, or equal to the PHI itself, return undef when at least one undef input was seen, otherwise poison.

When all non-self PHI inputs are one common value plus optional poison/undef, return the common value if it dominates the PHI; if undef inputs exist, also require the value is guaranteed non-poison. With only identical non-poison values, return the common value directly.
If all PHI incoming values are the same non-poison, non-undef SSA value (ignoring self references), replace the PHI with that value.
extra: all incoming values identical or self

description: For a constant source operand, fold the requested cast to its destination type using LLVM constant cast folding. Pointer-address/memory-dependent alternatives are separated as IS5681p.
Fold a nontrivial integer-to-pointer constant cast to the corresponding LLVM pointer ConstantExpr; this is the pointer-address constant alternative of the generic constant-cast fold.

Cancel a two-cast chain to its original source when LLVM's isEliminableCastPair says the pair is equivalent to a bitcast and the original source type equals the requested destination type. Pointer-address/memory-dependent alternatives are separated as IS5693p.

Cancel an eliminable integer/pointer round trip when isEliminableCastPair returns BitCast and the original source type equals the destination type; this entry isolates the memory-dependent pointer/integer alternatives.
A bitcast from a value to its identical type returns the operand.
Cancel ptrtoaddr(ptradd(Ptr, sub(X, ptrtoint-or-ptrtoaddr(Ptr)))) to X when X has the requested type and that type is the pointer's DataLayout index type.
Cancel zext(trunc(X)) to X when X has the final destination type and trunc has nuw; cancel sext(trunc(X)) under the same type condition when trunc has nsw.
An addrspacecast marked nonnull from null becomes poison when function context exists and null pointers are not defined in the source address space.

Recursively inspect the selected lane through nested fixed-vector shuffles; return the root source only when every selected root is the same SSA vector and the final lane equals the destination lane. An undef mask lane or recursion exhaustion prevents the fold.
Return the common root vector when the selected lane originates from that same vector and retains its lane number through the shuffle chain.
If every shuffle mask element is poison, the shuffle result is poison of the result vector type.
When both input vectors are constants, fold the shuffle constant expression using its mask.

For a non-scalable shuffle where Op0 is insertelement(_, constant C, constant InsertIndex), Op1 is undef, and every mask element is either InsertIndex or undef (-1), build a constant splat of C, replacing output lanes selected by undef mask entries with poison.
For shuffle(Op0, undef), return Op0 when Op0 is itself a shuffle, result type equals input vector type, and every inner shuffle mask lane is equal (a splat shuffle).
Return the common vector when every output lane is an identity lane recovered by foldIdentityShuffles across nested shuffle operands.
Delegate constant unary operation folding to LLVM ConstantFoldUnaryOpOperand; return null for nonconstant or unsupported constants.
Constant-fold fneg when the operand is constant.
Cancel fneg(fneg(X)) to X.
For fixed vectors, propagate poison elements; quiet existing NaNs while preserving their payload; replace other or unknown elements by canonical NaN, and return the rebuilt vector.
For a non-fixed-vector NaN constant that is not itself NaN, return canonical NaN of its type.
For scalar or scalable-vector NaN constants, preserve NaN sign/payload and quiet a signaling NaN; scalable input must be a NaN splat.
If any FP operation operand is poison, return poison of the first operand type.
With nnan, a NaN operand or undef operand yields poison of that operand's type.
With ninf, an infinite operand or undef operand yields poison of that operand's type.
In the default FP environment, an undef operand yields canonical NaN of its type.
extra: exception behavior and rounding mode must be default

description: In the default FP environment, propagate an input NaN constant through the operation via propagateNaN.
extra: exception behavior and rounding mode must be default

description: With non-strict constrained FP (exception behavior other than strict), propagate NaN constants via propagateNaN; strict exception behavior prevents this fold.
In the default FP environment, constant-fold/commute fadd operands when the constant folder succeeds.
Apply shared FP poison/undef/NaN simplifications to fadd before algebraic identities.
Fold fadd(X,-0.0) to X when signaling NaNs may be ignored and either rounding cannot be toward negative or nsz is set.
Fold fadd(X,+0.0) to X when signaling NaNs may be ignored and X cannot be negative zero or nsz is set.
With nnan in default FP environment, fadd(X,+/-Inf) returns the infinity operand.
With nnan, fold (-X)+X or X+(-X) to positive zero when either operand is a subtraction from either signed zero of the other operand.
With nnan, fold fadd(X,fneg(X)) or fadd(fneg(X),X) to positive zero.
With nsz and reassociation, fold (X-Y)+Y or Y+(X-Y) to X.
In the default FP environment, constant-fold/commute fsub operands when constant folding succeeds.
Apply shared FP poison/undef/NaN simplifications to fsub before algebraic identities.
Fold fsub(X,+0.0) to X when signaling NaNs may be ignored and either rounding cannot be toward negative or nsz is set.
Fold fsub(X,-0.0) to X when signaling NaNs may be ignored and X cannot be negative zero or nsz is set.
When signaling NaNs may be ignored, fold -0.0 - fneg(X) to X.
With nsz and signaling NaNs ignored, fold either signed zero minus (signed zero minus X) or fneg(X) to X.
With nnan in default FP environment, fsub(X,X) is positive zero.
With nnan in default FP environment, fsub(+/-Inf,X) returns the first infinite operand.
With nnan in default FP environment, fsub(X,+/-Inf) returns fneg of the infinite second operand.
With nsz and reassociation, fold Y-(Y-X) or (X+Y)-Y to X.
Apply shared FP poison/undef/NaN simplifications to fmul before identities.
Fold X*1.0 to X in the default FP environment.
Fold X*+/-0.0 to positive zero with both nnan and nsz.
If X is known finite and non-NaN and either nsz is set or sign is known nonnegative, simplify X*(+/-0) to +0 when nsz is set.
If X is known finite and non-NaN with known nonnegative sign and nsz is absent, simplify X*(+/-0) to the zero operand (preserving its sign).
If X is known finite and non-NaN with known negative sign and nsz is absent, simplify X*(+/-0) to fneg of the zero operand.
With reassoc, nnan, and nsz, fold sqrt(X)*sqrt(X) to X.
In the default FP environment, constant-fold/commute fmul operands when constant folding succeeds.
In the default FP environment, constant-fold/commute fdiv operands when constant folding succeeds.
Apply shared FP poison/undef/NaN simplifications to fdiv before identities.
In the default FP environment, fold X/1.0 to X.
With nnan and nsz in the default FP environment, fold 0/X to positive zero.
With nnan, fold X/X to 1.0.
With nnan and reassoc, fold (X*Y)/Y to X.
With nnan, fold (-X)/X or X/(-X) to -1.0.
With nnan and ninf, division by either signed zero yields poison.
In the default FP environment, constant-fold/commute frem operands when constant folding succeeds.
Apply shared FP poison/undef/NaN simplifications to frem before signed-zero identities.
With nnan, +0.0 % X simplifies to a full positive-zero constant, including vector elements.
With nnan, -0.0 % X simplifies to a full negative-zero constant, preserving frem dividend sign.

Resolve llvm.load.relative to the referenced GlobalValue when Ptr is a constant global plus offset, Offset is a constant integer no wider than 64 bits and divisible by four, the constant load decodes as (optionally trunc'd) ptrtoint(global) minus another constant global address, and both global symbol and offset match Ptr's symbol/offset.

The helper returns Op0 if either ldexp operand is poison; at the public simplifyIntrinsic entry, the prior intrinsicPropagatesPoison check converts poison in either argument to poison of the return type before reaching this helper.
ldexp(undef, x) yields NaN of the FP operand type.
For non-strict ldexp only, ldexp(x, undef) returns x.
For a constant FP first operand that is either signed zero or signed infinity, ldexp returns that operand even in strict mode.
For non-strict ldexp with NaN first operand, return the same NaN quieted (this branch is after strict mode was rejected).
For non-strict ldexp(x, 0), return x.
For any intrinsic classified idempotent, remove a repeated application when Op0 is an IntrinsicInst with the same intrinsic ID.
extra: applies to fabs, floor, ceil, trunc, rint, nearbyint, round, roundeven, canonicalize, arithmetic_fence

description: If the outer intrinsic removes fractional FP bits and Op0 is another such intrinsic or an integer-to-FP cast, eliminate the outer rounding operation.
extra: floor, ceil, trunc, rint, nearbyint, round, roundeven

description: fabs(X) returns X when value tracking proves X has a nonnegative sign bit.
fabs(X) returns X when X cannot be ordered below zero, is known non-NaN, and nsz is set.
Cancel bswap(bswap(X)) to X.
Cancel bitreverse(bitreverse(X)) to X.
Fold ctpop(X) to one when known-bits analysis proves X is a nonzero power of two.
Fold ctpop(X) to X when masked-value analysis proves every bit except the least significant bit is zero.
With reassoc, fold exp(log(X)) to X.
With reassoc, fold exp2(log2(X)) to X.
With reassoc, fold exp10(log10(X)) to X.
With reassoc, fold log(exp(X)) to X.
With reassoc, fold log2(exp2(X)) or log2(pow(2.0,X)) to X.
With reassoc, fold log10(exp10(X)) or log10(pow(10.0,X)) to X.
Cancel vector.reverse(vector.reverse(X)) to X.
vector.reverse(X) returns X when X is a vector splat.
llvm.structured.gep(X) returns its sole pointer operand unchanged.
For max/min nesting with shared X or Y, return the inner min/max call when the inner and outer intrinsic IDs match.
For max(min(X,Y),X) or the commuted/shared equivalent, return the shared operand when inner operation is inverse of outer operation.
For a minimum/maximum/minnum/maxnum/minimumnum/maximumnum call m(M0(X,Y),Z), return M0 when Z equals either inner operand.
For m(M0(X,Y),M1(X,Y)) with commuted inner operands allowed, return M0 when inner and outer intrinsic IDs match or are inverses.
For eorv/orv/saddv/uaddv/umaxv, return zero if predicate operand is all false or reduction operand is zero.
For andv/uminv, return all ones if predicate is all false or input is all ones.
For smaxv, return signed minimum if predicate is all false or input is signed minimum.
For sminv, return signed maximum if predicate is all false or input is signed maximum.
For andv/orv/smaxv/sminv/umaxv/uminv with all-true predicate, reduce a splat vector to its splat scalar value.
For eorv with all-true predicate, reducing a splat vector yields zero.
llvm.get.active.lane.mask(A,B) is false when B is zero.
If function has finite vscale maximum and return type is scalable, get.active.lane.mask(0, constant B) is all ones when B is at least min-lanes times maximum vscale.
Cancel nested llvm.abs(abs(X, flags), flags2) to the inner abs call, irrespective of nsw on the outer call.
Fold cttz(shl(1,X), is_zero_undef) to X.
Fold ctlz(lshr(-1,X), is_zero_undef) to X.
Fold ctlz(ashr(-1,X), is_zero_undef) to zero.
llvm.pdep(X,0) returns zero.
llvm.pdep(0,M) returns zero.
llvm.pdep(X, all_ones) returns X.
llvm.pext(X,0) returns zero.
llvm.pext(0,M) returns zero.
llvm.pext(X, all_ones) returns X.
llvm.ptrmask(undef,Mask) or llvm.ptrmask(null,Mask) returns null of pointer type.
llvm.ptrmask(Ptr,ptrtoint-or-ptrtoaddr(Ptr)) returns Ptr when mask width is exactly pointer index width.
llvm.ptrmask(Ptr,Mask) returns Ptr when Mask is all ones or undef; result attributes may be lost by this fold.
For an immediate constant ptrmask mask, compute known zero pointer bits and fold to Ptr when all bits cleared by the mask are already known zero from alignment.
For integer smax/smin/umax/umin, identical operands return the common operand.
`smax(X,undef) -> signed_max`, `smin(X,undef) -> signed_min`, `umax(X,undef) -> unsigned_max`, and `umin(X,undef) -> 0`, after moving an immediate constant to the right operand.

Clamp integer min/max to its absorbing extremum: `smax(X,signed_max) -> signed_max`, `smin(X,signed_min) -> signed_min`, `umax(X,unsigned_max) -> unsigned_max`, `umin(X,0) -> 0`. Either operand may be the constant; APInt matching permits poison vector lanes.

Remove the identity extremum: `smax(X,signed_min) -> X`, `smin(X,signed_max) -> X`, `umax(X,0) -> X`, `umin(X,unsigned_max) -> X`. Either operand may be the constant; APInt matching permits poison vector lanes.
For nested calls of the same integer min/max intrinsic, remove the outer call when an inner constant operand compares at least as extreme as the outer constant using the non-strict min/max predicate.
Apply foldMinMaxSharedOp in operand order (Op0,Op1) and return its result when non-null.
Apply foldMinMaxSharedOp in commuted operand order (Op1,Op0) and return its result when non-null.
For integer min/max, if value analysis proves Op0 <= Op1 (non-strict operation predicate), return Op0.
For integer min/max, if value analysis proves Op1 <= Op0 (non-strict operation predicate), return Op1.
For scmp/ucmp, return zero when equality between operands is proven.
For scmp/ucmp, return +1 when signed/unsigned greater-than is proven.
For scmp/ucmp, return -1 when signed/unsigned less-than is proven.
For umulh, or any mul-high operation on a one-bit result, multiplying by one yields zero.
For umulh/smulh, if either operand is undef, choose zero because the other operand may be zero.
For umulh/smulh, multiplication by zero yields zero.
For usub_with_overflow or ssub_with_overflow, X-X or either operand undef yields {0,false}.
For uadd_with_overflow or sadd_with_overflow, either operand undef yields {-1,false}.
For umul_with_overflow or smul_with_overflow, multiplying by zero yields {0,false}.
For umul_with_overflow or smul_with_overflow, either undef operand yields {0,false}.
For uadd_sat, adding all-ones to either operand yields all-ones.
For sadd_sat/uadd_sat, either undef operand yields all-ones; for signed add this chooses undef as bitwise complement of the other operand.
For signed or unsigned saturating add, X+0 returns X.
For signed or unsigned saturating add, 0+X returns X.
For usub_sat, 0-X or X-all_ones yields zero.
`ssub.sat X,X` and `usub.sat X,X` fold to zero. The undef alternatives sharing this return are IS7213u.
`ssub.sat` or `usub.sat` with either operand undef folds to zero.
For signed/unsigned saturating subtract, X-0 returns X.
For load_relative with two constant operands, return simplifyRelativeLoad's result if its constant relocation/load pattern matches.
For powi(X, constant zero), return 1.0.
For powi(X, constant one), return X.
Delegate ldexp to simplifyLdexp in non-strict mode.
For copysign(X,X), return X.
For copysign(-X,X) or copysign(X,-X), return the second operand.
For is_fpclass(X,mask), return true when mask contains every FP class flag.
For is_fpclass(X,mask), return false when mask contains no FP class flags.
For is_fpclass(undef,mask), return undef unless mask already matched the all-classes or no-classes cases.
For minnum/minimum/maxnum/maximum/minimumnum/maximumnum with identical operands, return the operand (ignoring NaN quieting).
For floating min/max with a constant operand, return the other operand when OptimizeConstMinMax classifies the constant as UseOtherVal or UseEither; this may ignore NaN quieting.
For floating min/max with a constant operand, return the constructed new constant when OptimizeConstMinMax classifies it UseNewConstVal; quiet NaNs as specified by intrinsic semantics.
Apply floating minimum/maximum shared-operand fold in (Op0,Op1) order.
Apply floating minimum/maximum shared-operand fold in commuted (Op1,Op0) order.
For vector_extract(vector_insert(Y,X,0),0), return X when constant extract index is zero and X's type equals the intrinsic return type.
Delegate recognized AArch64 SVE integer reductions to simplifySVEIntReduction.

Cancel interleaveN(extractvalue(deinterleaveN(X),0), …, extractvalue(deinterleaveN(X),N-1)) to X when arity equals factor, each single extract index equals its position, and all extracts use the same deinterleave intrinsic call of the matching factor.
If the intrinsic is defined to propagate poison and any argument is poison, return poison of the intrinsic return type.
When every intrinsic argument is constant, return the result of LLVM ConstantFoldIntrinsic if it succeeds.
For zero-operand vscale, return a constant when function context exists and getVScaleRange has a single known element.
Apply simplifyIdentityInterleave to all-arity interleave/deinterleave argument patterns and return its non-null result.
For one-argument intrinsics, delegate to simplifyUnaryIntrinsic with call fast-math flags and query.
For two-argument intrinsics, delegate to simplifyBinaryIntrinsic with intrinsic ID, return type, operands, flags, and query.
For masked_load or masked_gather with mask all zeros or poison, return passthrough argument Args[2].
For fshl/fshr with both data operands undef, return undef of the result type.
For fshl/fshr with undef shift amount, treat the shift as zero and return operand 0 for fshl or operand 1 for fshr.
For constant shift amount, reduce it modulo scalar bit width; if effective shift is zero return operand 0 for fshl or operand 1 for fshr.
Fold fshl((lshr X,C1),(shl X,C2),C1) or fshr((lshr X,C1),(shl X,C2),C2) to X when C1+C2 equals bit width and intrinsic shift amount equals C1 for fshl or C2 for fshr.
For fshl/fshr with both data operands zero, return zero for any shift amount.
For fshl/fshr with both data operands all ones, return all ones for any shift amount.
Delegate experimental_constrained_fma to shared simplifyFPOp using call exception behavior and rounding mode.
Delegate fma/fmuladd to shared simplifyFPOp under ignore-exceptions, nearest-ties-to-even environment.
For smul_fix/smul_fix_sat, canonicalize constants to operand 1 then return zero when that operand is zero.
For smul_fix/smul_fix_sat, return zero when canonicalized operand 1 is undef.
For smul_fix/smul_fix_sat, return operand 0 when operand 1 equals 1<<Scale, provided the one-bit constant is nonnegative at result width; Scale is the constant third operand.
For vector_insert(Y, vector_extract(X,0),0), return X when Y is undef or the same SSA vector as X, index is constant zero, and X type equals return type.
Fold vector_splice_right(vector_splice_left(poison,X,Offset),poison,Offset) to X when the inner offset is the identical SSA value and the right passthrough is poison.
For vector_splice_left/right, an undef offset yields poison of the result vector type.

For vector_splice_left/right, return poison when known unsigned minimum offset exceeds the maximum possible vector element count; scalable count uses function vscale range when available, otherwise full range.
For a proven zero splice offset, vector_splice_left(A,B,0) returns A and vector_splice_right(A,B,0) returns B.
Delegate constrained fadd to simplifyFAddInst with its FMF, exception behavior, and rounding mode.
Delegate constrained fsub to simplifyFSubInst with its FMF, exception behavior, and rounding mode.
Delegate constrained fmul to simplifyFMulInst with its FMF, exception behavior, and rounding mode.
Delegate constrained fdiv to simplifyFDivInst with its FMF, exception behavior, and rounding mode.
Delegate constrained frem to simplifyFRemInst with its FMF, exception behavior, and rounding mode.
Delegate constrained ldexp to simplifyLdexp in strict mode.
Cancel vp_reverse(vp_reverse(X, mask1, EVL), mask2, EVL) to X when both use the exact same EVL SSA operand; mask operands may differ.
For vp_reverse(X,mask,EVL), return X unchanged when X is a splat, regardless of mask or EVL.
extra: mask/EVL are irrelevant after splat proof

description: For gc.relocate, if either derived pointer or base pointer is undef, return undef of the relocation result type.
For gc.relocate returning pointer type, a null derived pointer becomes null of the result pointer type; this assumes most collectors preserve null relocation.
For other intrinsic calls, derive FP exception behavior and rounding from constrained call metadata (default ignore/nearest-even), then delegate to simplifyIntrinsic by intrinsic ID and return type.
When target library analysis says a direct callee can constant-fold and every non-metadata argument is a constant, return LLVM ConstantFoldCall result.
A call through undef or null callee yields poison of call result type, except musttail calls are rejected before this rule.
If tryConstantFoldCall succeeds, return its folded result.
For direct intrinsic callee (after call constant folding fails), invoke simplifyIntrinsic(CallBase) and return any non-null simplification.
For constrained FP call, first return the constant-folded result if tryConstantFoldCall succeeds.
For constrained FP call, return simplifyIntrinsic(CallBase) result when non-null after constant folding fails.
Remove freeze(X) and return X when value tracking proves X is neither undef nor poison.
For nonvolatile load from a constant pointer operand, constant-fold the loaded value from that pointer.

If underlying object is a constant global with definitive initializer and ConstantFoldLoadFromUniformValue proves initializer uniform for requested load type, return that constant regardless of offset.

Strip constant offsets through invariant.group while allowing inbounds relaxation; if stripped pointer is the constant global, sign-extend/truncate offset to that address space's index width and constant-fold load from the global initializer.
For any instruction whose NewOps are all constants and which has no explicit simplifier case, constant-fold the instruction operands; otherwise return null.
Dispatch FNeg instruction to simplifyFNegInst using instruction fast-math flags.
Dispatch FAdd instruction to simplifyFAddInst with instruction fast-math flags.
Dispatch Add with nsw/nuw flags from instruction-info query to simplifyAddInst.
Dispatch FSub instruction to simplifyFSubInst with instruction fast-math flags.
Dispatch Sub with nsw/nuw flags from instruction-info query to simplifySubInst.
Dispatch FMul instruction to simplifyFMulInst with instruction fast-math flags.
Dispatch Mul with nsw/nuw flags from instruction-info query to simplifyMulInst.
Dispatch SDiv with exact flag from instruction-info query to simplifySDivInst.
Dispatch UDiv with exact flag from instruction-info query to simplifyUDivInst.
Dispatch FDiv instruction to simplifyFDivInst with instruction fast-math flags.
Dispatch SRem instruction to simplifySRemInst.
Dispatch URem instruction to simplifyURemInst.
Dispatch FRem instruction to simplifyFRemInst with instruction fast-math flags.
Dispatch Shl with nsw/nuw flags from instruction-info query to simplifyShlInst.
Dispatch LShr with exact flag from instruction-info query to simplifyLShrInst.
Dispatch AShr with exact flag from instruction-info query to simplifyAShrInst.
Dispatch And instruction to simplifyAndInst.
Dispatch Or instruction to simplifyOrInst.
Dispatch Xor instruction to simplifyXorInst.
Dispatch ICmp using its predicate and two replacement operands to simplifyICmpInst.
Dispatch FCmp using its predicate, instruction fast-math flags, and replacement operands to simplifyFCmpInst.
Dispatch Select with condition, true/false replacement values, and fast-math flags (when select is FP math operator) to simplifySelectInst.
Dispatch GetElementPtr using original source element type and no-wrap flags with replacement pointer/index operands to simplifyGEPInst.
Dispatch InsertValue with original index path and replacement aggregate/value operands.
Dispatch InsertElement with replacement vector/value/index operands.
Dispatch ExtractValue with original aggregate index path and replacement aggregate operand.
Dispatch ExtractElement with replacement vector and index operands.
Dispatch ShuffleVector with original mask, result type, and replacement source vectors.
Dispatch PHI using replacement incoming values and original PHI node for dominance checks.
Dispatch Call with the replacement callee and replacement arguments after excluding operand bundle operands.
Dispatch Freeze to simplifyFreezeInst on the replacement operand.
Dispatch AddrSpaceCast with replacement operand, original result type, and nonnull property only when instruction info is enabled.
Dispatch every remaining cast opcode using replacement source operand and original destination type.
Dispatch Load using the original load instruction attributes and replacement pointer operand.
Public wrapper invokes internal instruction simplification with recursion limit after asserting replacement operand count matches instruction operand count.
Call simplifyInstructionWithOperands on the instruction's current operands; if unreachable-code simplification returns the instruction itself, return poison of its type.
